statement.essentials: Sweating and flushing over the cheek when eating is common after parotid surgery if you test for it, but fewer people notice it themselves.
statement.anatomy: Frey syndrome is diagnosed with the starch-iodine test: iodine is painted on the cheek, starch dusted over it and a lemon slice or sour drop given; the area of gustatory sweating stains dark blue.
statement.clinical: In 59 patients after unilateral parotidectomy, 20 (33.9%) reported symptoms after eating, while 30 (50.8%) tested positive on Minor's starch-iodine test; 19 of those 30 (63.3%) had symptoms, and 2 of 29 test-negative patients (6.9%) did. Pooled single-arm rates in pleomorphic adenoma were lower after extracapsular dissection (4%) than after superficial parotidectomy (13%).

limitations: One 59-patient series; the paper's own point is that the reported incidence varies widely with how Frey syndrome is measured. The pooled comparison after different operations is in claim ecd-vs-superficial-outcomes and is not a randomised comparison.
